newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow $68, off $1 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow $68, off $1 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle quietly traded at $68.00 in a light test, down $1.00 from the bulk of sales earlier in the week, feedlot sources said.
About 1,500 slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area. No sales were reported in Kansas.
However, fed cattle prices had been expected to drift lower amid sentiment that beef demand had peaked following two weeks of active buying.
Beef prices Friday were quoted down $0.20 to $0.36 per cwt, with 196 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Beef prices were quoted lower for the first time since April 9. Heavier-weight choice rose $7.34 in that time before slipping $0.22 to $106.37 Friday.
Fed cattle prices next week also could be pressured slightly by light packer demand following this week's brisk sales, which plumped live inventories, the sources said.
The light demand could offset potential support from outlooks for steady to lower showlists, compared with this week, they said.
Fed cattle cash reaction to Friday's USDA monthly Cattle-On-Feed report was seen as neutral.
The report was not expected to impact cash prices next week because USDA's estimate came in near trade expectations, market sources said.
USDA pegged cattle on-feed in the seven largest cattle producing states as of April 1 at 107 percent of a year ago, March placements at 102 and March marketings at 101.
Average pre-report analysts' estimates pegged on-feed at 107.6 percent, placements at 103.3 and marketings at 100.6.
